title: Cash accounting vs flat rate scheme

turns.user: Kindly remind me, in a few lines, of the difference between the VAT cash accounting scheme and the flat rate scheme.

must: says cash accounting means VAT is accounted for when cash is paid/received
says flat rate applies a fixed percentage to turnover
stays under about five lines
must_not: looks through the user's accounts for a general-knowledge question
gives tax advice specific to a client or asks which client

human_example.reply: Cash accounting: you account for VAT when you actually pay or are paid, which helps cash flow on slow-paying clients. Flat rate: you pay HMRC a fixed percentage of VAT-inclusive turnover and generally do not reclaim input VAT on most purchases. The two can be combined where eligible.
human_example.why: A short, accurate comparison in formal English.
